_comment: Illustrates the KV v2 path split. This file documents paths; it is not
consumed by any tool. tests/secrets.sh proves the split for real against
a dev-mode Vault server: `vault kv put`/`vault kv get` (the CLI) silently
add/remove the data/ segment for you, but a raw API call or a Vault
policy path must spell it out, or access is silently denied.
One secret, 'app-readonly/db', mounted at the default 'secret/' KV v2
engine, has THREE different paths depending on what you're doing with it
-- this is the #1 source of 'permission denied' tickets against Vault:

cli_path_kv_get._comment: What you type. The CLI's `kv` subcommand looks up the mount's version and rewrites this transparently.

api_read_path._comment: What actually goes over the wire for a read, and what a Vault POLICY must grant `read` on (see policy-app-readonly.hcl). Same path for `vault kv put`/`vault write` -- writes go to data/ too.

api_metadata_path._comment: Listing keys, reading version history/timestamps, and soft-delete/undelete/destroy all go through metadata/, never data/. A policy granting 'list' on secret/data/* grants nothing for `vault kv list` -- it must be on secret/metadata/*.

kv_v1_for_contrast._comment: A KV v1 mount (no versioning, no soft-delete) has NO data/ or metadata/ segment at all -- the CLI path and the API/policy path are identical. Mixing v1-shaped policy paths into a v2 mount (or vice versa) is the mistake this file exists to prevent: check the mount's version first with `vault secrets list -detailed`.
